issues.competing_evidence: Frew (2008, Appendix B.2) favors ambient low-excitation H II gas photoionized by disk/WD and a wind bow shock; Bond & Miszalski (2018, §6) allow chance ISM-cloud encounter or old nova ejecta; Castro Segura et al. (2021, §§3.6.1, 4.1) suggest a possible ~900-1000 yr shell from proper-motion back-projection; Iłkiewicz et al. (2026, §3.2, Fig. 3) report layered W2/H-alpha morphology, favor wind/ISM structure, but explicitly cannot exclude a shell.
issues.why_it_matters: A shell identification affects nova recurrence and evolutionary comparisons; current evidence does not establish one origin.
issues.needed_action: Keep origin unresolved. Future expansion/kinematic and abundance measurements, especially nitrogen, are needed to distinguish ejecta from ambient gas/wind cavity.

issues.competing_evidence: Bond & Miszalski (2018) report 0.15216 +/-0.00002 d = 3.65184 +/-0.00048 h from 2006 H-alpha RVs. Castro Segura et al. (2021) combine 2006, 2017 and 2018 RVs across ~27000 cycles and report 0.15220606(6) d = 3.6529454 +0.0000016/-0.0000013 h. The ~3.98 s difference is ~2.3 times the older formal error; Castro Segura say separate-season estimates agree within errors.
issues.why_it_matters: The orbital clock controls phase, velocity-derived q, and period-dependent population comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Retain both values and provisionally use the long-baseline combined ephemeris. Reconcile per-season velocities, aliases, epoch convention and covariance before calling the old value discrepant or superseded.

issues.competing_evidence: Castro Segura et al. (2021) report q=M2/M1=0.51 +/-0.03(stat) +0.4/-0.2(sys), depending on donor irradiation correction and disk-shadow geometry. An expected sequence donor M2≈0.26 Msun gives M1≈0.5 Msun (≈0.55 Msun with no shadowing); authors say the low result suggests K velocities may be proxies and needs confirmation. Hewitt et al. (2020) Table 4 assumes M1=0.75 and M2=0.27 Msun for SED.
issues.why_it_matters: Treating a sequence/model inference as a WD mass measurement would bias WD-mass and evolutionary comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Keep q with separate statistical/systematic errors and leave the wide-table WD mass blank pending independent donor absorption or dynamical constraints.

issues.competing_evidence: Native 2SXPS row 187732 gives 0.3-10 keV observed flux 1.309e-12 and power-law-unabsorbed flux 1.58e-12 erg cm-2 s-1. Ridder et al. (2023) convert to 1-10 keV 1.2 +/-0.2e-12 and 0.1-10 keV 1.5 +/-0.3e-12, but Table 4 does not mark absorbed/unabsorbed. Castro Segura et al. (2021) separately fit two Swift epochs with a low-count two-component model.
issues.why_it_matters: Absorption and spectral model affect comparison of X-ray output across CVs, WD pulsars and transients.
issues.needed_action: Keep native observed/unabsorbed 2SXPS and Ridder comparison fluxes separate. Verify exact model/conversion inputs and absorbed convention before selecting one comparison flux.

issues.competing_evidence: Frew (2008) derives nebular E(B-V)=0.04 +/-0.04 from Fr 2-11's Balmer decrement and reports total-to-infinity map E(B-V)=0.144. Neither is a binary-specific Gaia correction; Gaia photometry is unresolved variable accretion-system light. M_G is retained without extinction and BP-RP is observed.
issues.why_it_matters: Reddening choices change intrinsic CMD color and extinction-corrected M_G and may not describe the unresolved binary.
issues.needed_action: Leave intrinsic color and extinction-corrected M_G blank until an applicable source-specific reddening and extinction law are justified; record whether nebular decrement is applicable to the binary.

issues.competing_evidence: Frew (2008) Appendix B.2.1 prose reports log F(H-beta)=-11.4 erg cm-2 s-1, corresponding to 3.98e-12 erg cm-2 s-1. Table B.1 footnote on the same printed page reports F(H-beta)=1.05e-14 erg cm-2 s-1 with c(H-beta)=0.06. These differ by about 379x. The prose value gives H-alpha/H-beta≈2.8 using the prose log F(H-alpha)=-10.95, consistent with the stated intrinsic Balmer ratio; the footnote value does not. Both original-text claims are visually checked; neither is silently preferred.
issues.why_it_matters: The Balmer decrement supports the cited E(B-V) and nebular interpretation. Choosing the wrong integrated flux would misstate nebular brightness and potentially undermine reddening provenance.
issues.needed_action: Keep both claims separately ledgered. Verify against the thesis source image/original reduced SHASSA measurement or a Frew erratum/author clarification; determine whether Table B.1 value has a transcription, exponent, or aperture-definition issue before adopting a single integrated flux.
